    StartersNumidian honey-fried stuffed datesMedjool dates with almond and pepper, fried in butter and honeyHow to make it24 Medjool dates24 whole almonds30g butter3 tbsp honeysea salt flakes, to tasteToast the whole almonds in a dry pan for 4 minutes.Slit and pit the Medjool dates, push an almond and a grind of black pepper into each and press closed.Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the dates 2 minutes, turning, until warm and glossy.Add the honey and let it bubble for 1 minute, turning the dates to coat.Tip onto a plate and sprinkle with flaky salt.Macrinus's baked feta with figs and honeyBaked feta with olives, figs, oregano and chilli, crusty breadHow to make it200g feta block150g mixed olives4 fresh figsolive oil, to tastedried oregano, to tastechilli flakes, to taste1 bunch thyme2 tbsp honey1 crusty loafHeat the oven to 200°C.Put the block of feta in a small baking dish with the mixed olives around it.Halve the fresh figs and nestle them in.Drizzle with the olive oil and sprinkle with dried oregano, chilli flakes and thyme sprigs.Bake 15 minutes until the feta is soft.Drizzle with the honey and serve with torn crusty bread.Bread and circuses rosemary flatbreadBread for the Colosseum crowdHow to make itAs written, serves 4Thin flatbreads blistered in a hot pan, brushed with garlic and rosemary oil, sprinkled with sea salt and served with labneh for dipping.Mix 300g self-raising flour, 250g Greek yoghurt and half a tsp salt into a dough and rest 10 minutes.Warm 4 tbsp olive oil with 2 sliced garlic cloves and 1 tbsp chopped rosemary for 3 minutes.Divide the dough into 8, roll thin and cook in a hot dry pan 1 to 2 minutes a side until charred in spots.Brush with the rosemary oil and sprinkle with flaky salt.Serve with 250g labneh drizzled with oil.Lamb meatballs with mint yoghurtMacrinus feeds his fighters well, then he bets.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsEmperors' honey roast chickenWhole roast chicken glazed with honey on a bed of carrotsHow to make it1.8kg whole chicken1 garlic bulb1 bunch thyme1 lemon6 carrots3 tbsp honeyRub the whole chicken with oil, salt, crushed garlic and thyme and stuff with a halved lemon.Roast at 200°C on a bed of the carrots for 60 minutes, then brush with the honey and roast 15 minutes more until sticky.Rest 10 minutes and carve.Numidian lamb, apricot and chickpea stewThe Roman siege of NumidiaHow to make itAs written, serves 4Lamb shoulder braised with chickpeas, tomato, cumin, cinnamon and dried apricots, spooned over fluffy couscous with harissa yoghurt and mint.Brown 1kg diced lamb shoulder in batches in oil.Fry 2 onions for 5 minutes, add 3 garlic cloves, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp cinnamon and 1 tsp paprika.Add 400g tinned tomatoes, 500ml stock and the lamb, cover and simmer 1.5 hours.Add 400g drained chickpeas and 120g dried apricots and cook 30 minutes.Pour 300ml boiling stock over 300g couscous, cover 5 minutes.Swirl 1 tbsp harissa through 200g yoghurt.Serve with mint.SweetsRoman honey cheesecakeBaked ricotta and honey cheesecake with lemon zestHow to make it500g ricotta3 eggs6 tbsp honey1 lemonBeat the ricotta with the eggs, the honey and the zest of the lemon until smooth.Pour into a lined 20cm tin and bake at 170°C for 40 minutes until just set.Cool and drizzle with more honey.DrinksEmperors' spiced honey wineWarm red wine with honey, cinnamon, pepper, bay and orange peelHow to make it750ml red wine4 tbsp honey1 cinnamon stickblack peppercorns, to tastebay leaves, to taste1 orangePour the bottle of red wine into a saucepan with the honey, the cinnamon stick, the black peppercorns, the bay leaves and the strips of orange peel.Warm gently over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring until the honey dissolves.Do not let it boil.Strain into heavy cups.For non-drinkers, make it the same way with red grape juice and less honey.Pomegranate and mint coolerLucius fought a rhino.
